comparison: Both evaluate replication timing claims (C8, C67-C71, C84) but reach opposite conclusions. OpenEval finds the evidence SUPPORTED with appropriate controls, while peer reviewers rate it UNSUPPORTED, arguing that S-phase defects confound interpretation and that experiments cannot distinguish heterochromatin-mediated effects from indirect ORC effects.

Both evaluate the proteotuner/degron experiments (C72-C78) showing independence from preRC function. OpenEval finds evidence SUPPORTED, while peer reviewers rate it UNCERTAIN, noting Figure 8 is 'very key' but lacks critical details about ORC binding validation, complementation controls, and biological significance of observed phenotypes.

Both evaluate H3K9 methylation state binding preference (C52, C53, C82). OpenEval and peer reviewers agree these claims are SUPPORTED, with no specific concerns raised about the peptide pulldown and SiMPull data showing ORCA's preferential binding to H3K9me3.

Both evaluate the feed-forward spreading model (C85, C86, C96, C100, C101). OpenEval rates it UNCERTAIN, noting the model is speculative and lacks direct evidence for spreading dynamics. Peer reviewers also rate it UNCERTAIN, questioning whether data support the model and suggesting alternative predictions to test it.

Both evaluate H3K9me3 changes upon ORCA depletion (C6, C7, C54-C57). OpenEval finds evidence SUPPORTED, explaining the apparent Western vs ChIP-seq discrepancy as site-specific effects. Peer reviewers rate it UNCERTAIN, identifying this as a critical unresolved discrepancy that undermines confidence in conclusions.

Both evaluate domain mapping and chromatin context-dependence (C37-C40, C42). OpenEval finds evidence SUPPORTED with elegant CLTon experiments. Peer reviewers also rate it SUPPORTED, raising no specific concerns about these domain mapping findings.

Both evaluate SiMPull stoichiometry and complex composition claims (C4, C46-C51). OpenEval finds evidence SUPPORTED with rigorous single-molecule analysis. Peer reviewers rate it UNCERTAIN, expressing significant concerns about transient transfections, first-time use of three-protein colocalization, and requesting additional corroborating methods like FRET or IP/re-IP.

Both evaluate ORCA's scaffold function (C5, C62-C66, C79). OpenEval finds evidence SUPPORTED through loss- and gain-of-function experiments. Peer reviewers rate it UNCERTAIN (in R2 and R3), requesting direct demonstration that ORCA depletion disrupts G9a/Suv39H1 co-IP and expressing concerns about overexpression artifacts.

Both evaluate endogenous co-IP evidence for ORCA-KMT interactions (C27-C29, C31). OpenEval finds evidence SUPPORTED with multiple orthogonal approaches. Peer reviewers rate it UNCERTAIN, noting poor quality and labeling in Figure 1Aa/Ab, requesting better antibodies and quantification to distinguish complex from free protein.

Overlapping evaluation of direct binding and DNA-independence (C3, C35, C36). OpenEval (R1) finds EtBr/benzonase experiments support DNA-independent interaction. Peer reviewers (R8) rate UNCERTAIN, noting chromatin-dependent data in Figure 2E is 'not easily reconciled' with direct binding claims and suggesting direct interactions may be too weak to detect in cells.

Both address ORCA ChIP and KMT recruitment (C58-C61). OpenEval includes these in broader SUPPORTED evaluation of site-specific effects. Peer reviewers separately rate these specific ChIP claims as SUPPORTED with no concerns raised.

Partial overlap on scaffold claims (C9, C81). OpenEval (R9) rates model/interpretation as UNCERTAIN. Peer reviewers (R3) also rate UNCERTAIN, specifically requesting demonstration that ORCA depletion disrupts G9a/Suv39H1 co-IP to establish scaffolding role definitively.

Both evaluate background/context claims from prior literature (C1, C11-C17). OpenEval and peer reviewers agree these are SUPPORTED as appropriately cited established facts providing context for the study.

Both evaluate additional background claims (C18-C26). OpenEval and peer reviewers agree these are SUPPORTED as well-established, appropriately cited facts from literature, particularly the multimeric complex findings from Fritsch et al. 2010.

Partial overlap on discussion/context claims (C87, C89-C95). OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN due to C88 claiming Suv420H1/H2 interaction with 'data not shown.' Peer reviewers rate the broader context claims as SUPPORTED, not challenging these background statements.

Minor overlap on chromatin context claims (C41, C43). OpenEval (R2) finds CLTon experiments elegantly demonstrate chromatin context-dependence. Peer reviewers (R8) question reconciliation with direct binding data, suggesting chromatin-dependent effects indicate weak direct interactions.

Minimal overlap on comparison to Fritsch et al. (C30). OpenEval finds this SUPPORTED as useful context for ORCA co-IP efficiency. Peer reviewers include this in broader SUPPORTED evaluation of background claims without specific comment.

OpenEval evaluates summary statements (C80, C83) as SUPPORTED, noting 'global' may be overstated given only 18% of peaks affected. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific summary claims.
